title: Carpet Padding Explained: Thickness, Density and Why It Matters More Than the Carpet
meta: Carpet padding explained: why 8 lb density beats extra thickness, which pad fits berber, plush and stairs, and what Edmonds homes need. From Wills Flooring.
keywords: carpet padding explained, carpet pad thickness and density, best carpet padding, 8 lb vs 6 lb carpet pad, rebond carpet pad, carpet pad for stairs, carpet installation Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: For most Edmonds bedrooms and living rooms, the right pad is a 7/16 in thick, 8 lb density rebond cushion. Density is what makes carpet last; thickness is what makes it feel soft, and past 1/2 in it starts to hurt the carpet.
blocks.detail: Berber and other looped carpets need a firmer, thinner pad, stairs need the firmest pad you can get, and any carpet over a slab near the water in Edmonds should sit on a pad with a moisture barrier.

blocks.html: Carpet padding is the part of the job nobody sees and almost everyone under-buys. When we pull up a 15-year-old carpet in a Seaview or Westgate rambler, the carpet itself is often still intact; it is the pad underneath that has turned to crumbs, and the carpet has been wearing against bare plywood for years. A common Reddit thread asks whether upgrading the pad is worth it or just an upsell. It is worth it, and here is exactly which numbers to look for so you buy the right pad once.

items.title: It absorbs the impact, not the carpet
items.text: Every footstep compresses the carpet fibers. With a good pad underneath, the pad takes most of that compression and springs back; the fibers bend less and recover faster. With a thin or worn pad, the fibers crush against the subfloor and mat down in traffic lanes within a few years. Most carpet warranties quietly assume a decent pad.

items.title: It quiets the room and the floor below
items.text: Pad is the main reason carpeted upstairs bedrooms in a two-story Perrinville house are so much quieter than the hardwood downstairs. Denser pad blocks more footfall noise and helps condo owners in the Edmonds Bowl meet building sound rules. A cheap 5 lb pad does much less here than an 8 lb one at the same thickness.

items.title: It insulates over cold floors
items.text: Over a slab, or over a crawlspace in a 1960s rambler, pad adds a real thermal break. Rebond and fiber pads trap air; rubber pads less so. If a room has always felt cold underfoot in winter, the pad you choose will change that more than the carpet fiber will, and it costs far less than heating the crawlspace.

items.title: It can stop spills from reaching the subfloor
items.text: Standard rebond is a sponge; pet accidents soak through into plywood and come back as odor for years. A pad with a moisture barrier film on top keeps liquid on the surface where it can be extracted. Our damp marine air makes this more useful, not less, because wet subfloors dry slowly.

blocks.text: The pad types you will be offered

items.html: Rebond (bonded urethane). The multicolored foam made from recycled cushion scraps. It is the standard for good reason: durable, affordable, available in every density. 8 lb, 7/16 in rebond is our default recommendation for living areas.

Frothed and memory foam. Denser, more uniform urethane. Frothed foam is very durable and thin; memory foam feels luxurious but can feel too soft for berber and slows carpet recovery. Good in bedrooms, skip it on stairs.
Fiber pad (synthetic felt). Firm and flat, often 3/8 in. This is the right pad under berber and commercial loop, and under many wool carpets. It does not feel plush, which is the point.

Rubber (waffle or flat slab). Premium and long-lived. Flat rubber is excellent under wool and on stairs. Waffle rubber feels soft because of the air pockets and can break down faster than flat. Both are heavier to handle.
Moisture-barrier rebond. Regular rebond with a sealed film face. Our most common upgrade for homes with dogs and for slab-floor rooms near the waterfront.

blocks.text: Match the pad to the carpet, not the other way around

a.title: Use a cushioned pad
items: 7/16 in rebond at 8 lb for family rooms and bedrooms
Memory foam is acceptable in low-traffic bedrooms
Moisture barrier if there are pets or young children
Keep it under 1/2 in so seams and stretch hold

b.tag: Loop pile: berber, level loop, many wools
b.title: Use a firm, thin pad
items: 3/8 in at 8 lb, or a fiber or flat rubber pad
Thick soft pads let loops stretch, causing rippling and pulled seams
Most berber warranties specify the thinner pad
Firm pad also helps loops resist snagging at the seams

blocks.text: Where Edmonds homes go wrong with pad

items.text: It looks fine, so the installer leaves it. Old pad has already lost its resilience where people walk, so the new carpet inherits the old traffic lanes within a year. New carpet always gets new pad, and old pad should be hauled away with the old carpet.

A thick, cushy pad on a Seaview split-level staircase feels great for a month. Then the carpet loosens at the nosing and starts to wrinkle. Stairs get a firm 8 lb pad or flat rubber, stretched tight over each tread.

items.d: Standard pad over a damp slab
items.text: Many 1950s to 1970s ramblers here have a slab-floor family room or a lower level that runs damp in winter. Ordinary rebond wicks that moisture up into the carpet and smells within a season. Test the slab, then use a barrier pad or a different floor entirely.

Buildings in the Bowl and near the ferry often require a minimum sound rating for floor coverings. A dense pad is the cheapest way to meet it. Ask the HOA for the number before choosing the pad, not after the neighbor complains.

blocks.title: Do not judge pad by squeezing it:
blocks.text: The softest sample in the store is usually the lowest density and the first to fail. Turn the sample over, read the density in pounds, and pick 8 lb. If the label only lists thickness, ask more questions. We bring pad samples with the carpet samples to every carpet estimate so you can compare labels side by side.

faq.q: Is 8 lb carpet pad worth it over 6 lb?
faq.a: Yes for any room people walk through daily. The 8 lb pad keeps its bounce for the life of the carpet, while 6 lb pad tends to flatten in traffic lanes after several years and the carpet wears faster there. The price difference is small relative to the whole job, and it protects the larger investment in the carpet.

Not past a point. Thickness adds softness, but carpet installed over pad thicker than 1/2 in flexes too much, stretches, and can wrinkle or pull at seams. Most carpet warranties cap pad at 7/16 or 1/2 in. Choose density for durability and keep thickness at 7/16 in for cut pile and 3/8 in for loops.

faq.q: What is the best carpet pad for stairs?
faq.a: A firm, dense pad: 8 lb rebond at 3/8 to 7/16 in, or flat rubber. Stairs take the most concentrated wear in the house and a soft pad lets the carpet shift on the nosing. The pad should also be fastened to each tread, not run loose down the staircase.

faq.q: Do I need a moisture barrier pad?
faq.a: You need one if you have dogs or cats, small children, or a slab floor. The barrier keeps accidents and spills on top of the pad where they can be blotted and extracted instead of soaking into the subfloor. In Edmonds homes with a damp lower level it also slows moisture from below.

faq.q: Can carpet pad be reused when installing new carpet?
faq.a: It should not be. Pad loses resilience exactly where people walked on the old carpet, so the new carpet would sit on a floor that is already uneven. New carpet should always go over new pad, and a proper installation includes removing and disposing of the old pad along with the old carpet.

faq.q: What pad goes under berber carpet?
faq.a: A thin, firm one: 3/8 in at 8 lb density, or a fiber or flat rubber pad. Berber is a loop pile that stretches and ripples over soft, thick cushion, and many berber warranties require the thinner pad. If you want a soft step under a loop carpet, choose a denser pad rather than a thicker one.
